analysis.investment_thesis: Clean Science is a rare zero-debt specialty chemical compounder with exceptional 24% operating margins and 27% ROE — balance sheet quality I deeply respect. However, the business has not surpassed its 2023 revenue/profit peak even by FY25, the current P/E of 33x is above my comfort ceiling, and China competition in specialty chemicals is a structural threat I cannot ignore.
key_strengths: Fortress balance sheet — borrowings of just INR 2 Cr against INR 1,500 Cr equity; D/E effectively zero
Exceptional profitability metrics: 24% operating margin, 61% gross margin, 27.3% ROCE — true pricing power
7-year revenue CAGR of 22% and net profit CAGR of 27.2% demonstrate compounding quality
key_risks: Revenue peaked at INR 936 Cr in FY23, fell to INR 791 Cr in FY24, only partially recovered to INR 967 Cr in FY25 — earnings momentum is broken
P/E of 32.8x and EV/EBITDA of 20.4x price in perfection; any further demand softness will compress the multiple sharply
Specialty chemicals face aggressive Chinese overcapacity — MEHQ, BHA, TBHQ are globally traded commodities at heart
red_flags: Net profit declined from INR 295 Cr (FY23) to INR 244 Cr (FY24) — a 17% drop from peak, still below FY23 in FY25
Free cash flow was near-zero in FY24 (INR 10 Cr) and INR 72 Cr in FY25 despite INR 264 Cr of net profit — heavy capex consuming cash
Promoter at 50.96% is slightly below my preferred 55% floor
analysis.detailed_analysis: Clean Science is everything I admire in a business — a focused producer of niche chemicals with near-zero debt, high returns, and consistent margin discipline. The FY18-FY23 compounding story was exceptional. But a business that earns less in FY25 than it did in FY23 is telling me something: either the end-market demand cycle has turned or competition is arriving, and at 33x earnings I am paying for resumed growth that has not yet materialised. I require a margin of safety, and this stock does not offer one at current prices.
